data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kamakya is the name of a goddess, often depicted holding a lotus in each hand. She represents desire and is believed to grant wishes. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Kama’, meaning desire, and ‘Kya’, meaning Goddess. The name Kamakya carries the meaning “Goddess of desire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kamakya usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kamakya total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In the Hindu culture, Kamakya is often venerated and worshiped in various parts of India, especially in states like Assam, Tripura, and West Bengal. She is also considered an important goddess in the Shakti tradition, where deities are predominantly female goddesses. Her story is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and has influenced art, music, and literature over centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Kamakya represents the power of desire and attraction. She is believed to fulfill the deepest desires of her devotees, helping them to overcome bindings of maya (illusion), and ultimately, achieve self-realization. Her significance lies in her role as a manifestation of the divine potency or shakti, which is an integral part of the Hindu concept of godhead.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kamakya signifies the embodiment of desire and passion in Hinduism. It is the name of a goddess revered for fulfilling deepest longings and desires, symbolizing the primal, untamed energy of the universe.

historical_references.reference: Kamakya is an important goddess in the Shakta tradition of Hinduism, often identified with the Goddess Kali or Tara. She is believed to have originated in the eastern Indian state of Assam, where she is still worshipped in temples.
historical_references.context: The Shakta tradition of Hinduism emphasizes the worship of the Goddess as the supreme deity and Kamakya is one of the major goddesses in this tradition. While her origins are unclear, she is believed to have originated in Assam, where she is still widely worshipped.

historical_references.reference: Kamakya is also known as Kamrupaswani, Kamakhya Devi, or Kamakhya Mata. She is believed to have a yoni pitha (sacred vaginal symbol) and is associated with fertility, sexuality, and motherhood.
historical_references.context: Kamakya is one of the major goddesses in Shaktism, a branch of Hinduism that emphasizes the worship of the goddess as the supreme deity. Her association with a yoni pitha and her role as a fertility goddess have made her an important deity in Hindu mythology and worship.

In modern contexts, Kamakya is seen on various platforms including social media, where devotees share pictures, stories, and videos related to the goddess and her temples. Another platform is festivals, particularly the annual Ambubachi Mela at the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati, Assam, which attracts thousands of pilgrims from across India and beyond.
